sanskrit: atra viśve sadā devāḥ pitṛbhiḥ sārdham āsate ijyamānāḥ sma lokeṣu saṃprāptās tulyabhāgatām
english: Here the Viśvedevas always dwell together with the ancestors; being worshipped in the worlds, they have attained an equal share of the oblations.

sanskrit: etad dvitīyaṃ dharmasya dvāram ācakṣate dvija truṭiśo lavaśaś cātra gaṇyate kālaniścayaḥ
english: This, O twice-born, is declared to be the second gate of righteousness; here the reckoning of time is counted in the smallest fractions of a moment.

sanskrit: atra devarṣayo nityaṃ pitṛlokarṣayas tathā tathā rājarṣayaḥ sarve nivasanti gatavyathāḥ
english: Here divine sages dwell perpetually, and likewise the sages of the ancestors' realm, and all the royal sages, free from sorrow.

sanskrit: atra dharmaś ca satyaṃ ca karma cātra niśāmyate gatir eṣā dvijaśreṣṭha karmaṇātmāvasādinaḥ
english: Here dharma and truth are observed, and deeds are witnessed; this is the path, O foremost of twice-born, for one whose self is brought low by its own actions.

sanskrit: eṣā dik sā dvijaśreṣṭha yāṃ sarvaḥ pratipadyate vṛtā tv anavabodhena sukhaṃ tena na gamyate
english: This is that direction, O foremost of twice-born, which all must enter; yet being shrouded in ignorance, it cannot be traversed in happiness.

sanskrit: nairṛtānāṃ sahasrāṇi bahūny atra dvijarṣabha sṛṣṭāni pratikūlāni draṣṭavyāny akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: Here, O bull among twice-born, thousands of demons have been let loose and adverse things must be seen by those who have not mastered themselves.

sanskrit: atra mandarakuñjeṣu viprarṣisadaneṣu ca gandharvā gānti gāthā vai cittabuddhiharā dvija
english: Here in the groves of Mandara and in the dwellings of seer-sages, the Gandharvas sing songs that captivate the heart and mind, O twice-born.

sanskrit: atra sāmāni gāthābhiḥ śrutvā gītāni raivataḥ gatadāro gatāmātyo gatarājyo vanaṃ gataḥ
english: Here, having heard the Sāma hymns sung together with ballads, Raivata abandoned wife, ministers, and kingdom and went to the forest.

sanskrit: atra sāvarṇinā caiva yavakrītātmajena ca maryādā sthāpitā brahman yāṃ sūryo nātivartate
english: Here a boundary was established by Sāvarṇi and the son of Yavakrīta, O brahmin, which even the sun does not transgress.

sanskrit: atra rākṣasarājena paulastyena mahātmanā rāvaṇena tapaś cīrtvā surebhyo 'maratā vṛtā
english: Here the great-souled king of the rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa, son of Pulastya, having performed austerities, chose immortality over the gods.

sanskrit: atra vṛttena vṛtro 'pi śakraśatrutvam īyivān atra sarvāsavaḥ prāptāḥ punar gacchanti pañcadhā
english: Here Vṛtra too, by his conduct, attained enmity with Indra; here all vital breaths, once spent, return and again disperse fivefold.

sanskrit: atra duṣkṛtakarmāṇo narāḥ pacyanti gālava atra vaitaraṇī nāma nadī vitaraṇair vṛtā atra gatvā sukhasyāntaṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ prapadyate
english: Here, O Gālava, men of evil deeds are tormented; here is the river named Vaitaraṇī, surrounded by those who help in crossing; having gone there, one reaches the end of happiness and the end of sorrow.

sanskrit: atrāvṛtto dinakaraḥ kṣarate surasaṃ payaḥ kāṣṭhāṃ cāsādya dhāniṣṭhāṃ himam utsṛjate punaḥ
english: Here the sun, turning back, pours out the nectar of the gods; having reached the point of the Dhaniṣṭhā constellation, it releases frost once more.

sanskrit: atrāhaṃ gālava purā kṣudhārtaḥ paricintayan labdhavān yudhyamānau dvau bṛhantau gajakacchapau
english: Here I, O Gālava, in a former time, tormented by hunger and deliberating, found two great creatures locked in battle — an elephant and a tortoise.

sanskrit: atra śakradhanur nāma sūryāj jāto mahān ṛṣiḥ vidur yaṃ kapilaṃ devaṃ yenāttāḥ sagarātmajāḥ
english: Here the great sage named Śakradhanus was born from the sun; they know him as the divine Kapila, by whom the sons of Sagara were consumed.

sanskrit: atra siddhāḥ śivā nāma brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ adhītya sakhilān vedān ālabhante yamakṣayam
english: Here dwell perfected brahmins called Śiva who have mastered the Vedas; having studied the entire corpus of the Vedas, they attain the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: atra bhogavatī nāma purī vāsukipālitā takṣakeṇa ca nāgena tathaivairāvatena ca
english: Here is the city named Bhogavatī, guarded by Vāsuki, and likewise by the serpent Takṣaka and by Airāvata.

sanskrit: atra niryāṇakāleṣu tamaḥ saṃprāpyate mahat abhedyaṃ bhāskareṇāpi svayaṃ vā kṛṣṇavartmanā
english: Here at the time of departing, a great darkness is encountered that cannot be pierced even by the sun or by fire, which travels on the dark path.

sanskrit: eṣa tasyāpi te mārgaḥ paritāpasya gālava brūhi me yadi gantavyaṃ pratīcīṃ śṛṇu vā mama
english: This too is the path of your anguish, O Gālava; tell me whether we should go west, or else listen to me.

sanskrit: suparṇa uvāca iyaṃ dig dayitā rājño varuṇasya tu gopateḥ sadā salilarājasya pratiṣṭhā cādir eva ca
english: Suparṇa said: This direction is the beloved realm of King Varuṇa, lord of the waters, always the foundation and very source of the king of the sea.

sanskrit: atra paścād ahaḥ sūryo visarjayati bhāḥ svayam paścimety abhivikhyātā dig iyaṃ dvijasattama
english: Here the sun releases its own light behind the day; this direction is renowned as the west, O foremost of twice-born.

sanskrit: yādasām atra rājyena salilasya ca guptaye kaśyapo bhagavān devo varuṇaṃ smābhyaṣecayat
english: Here the blessed divine Kaśyapa anointed Varuṇa with sovereignty over the creatures of the water and to guard the waters.

sanskrit: atra pītvā samastān vai varuṇasya rasāṃs tu ṣaṭ jāyate taruṇaḥ somaḥ śuklasyādau tamisrahā
english: Here, having drunk all six essences of Varuṇa, the young Moon is born at the start of the bright fortnight, destroyer of darkness.

sanskrit: atra paścāt kṛtā daityā vāyunā saṃyatās tadā niḥśvasanto mahānāgair arditāḥ suṣupur dvija
english: Here the demons were formerly bound by the wind; gasping and tormented by great serpents, they fell into deep sleep, O twice-born.

sanskrit: atra sūryaṃ praṇayinaṃ pratigṛhṇāti parvataḥ asto nāma yataḥ saṃdhyā paścimā pratisarpati
english: Here the mountain named Asta receives the devoted sun; it is from here that the western twilight creeps forth.

sanskrit: ato rātriś ca nidrā ca nirgatā divasakṣaye jāyate jīvalokasya hartum ardham ivāyuṣaḥ
english: From here night and sleep emerge at the close of day, arising as if to take away half the life of the living world.

sanskrit: atra devīṃ ditiṃ suptām ātmaprasavadhāriṇīm vigarbhām akaroc chakro yatra jāto marudgaṇaḥ
english: Here Indra caused the goddess Diti to miscarry while she slept, bearing within her the offspring of her own self; from that act the host of Maruts was born.

sanskrit: atra mūlaṃ himavato mandaraṃ yāti śāśvatam api varṣasahasreṇa na cāsyānto 'dhigamyate
english: Here the root of Himavat reaches eternally to Mount Mandara; even in a thousand years its end cannot be reached.

sanskrit: atra kāñcanaśailasya kāñcanāmbuvahasya ca udadhes tīram āsādya surabhiḥ kṣarate payaḥ
english: Here, reaching the shore of the ocean by the golden mountain and the river of golden water, the divine cow Surabhī pours out her milk.

sanskrit: atra madhye samudrasya kabandhaḥ pratidṛśyate svarbhānoḥ sūryakalpasya somasūryau jighāṃsataḥ
english: Here in the midst of the ocean the headless trunk of Svarbhānu is seen, that sun-like being who seeks to devour the sun and the moon.

sanskrit: suvarṇaśiraso 'py atra hariromṇaḥ pragāyataḥ adṛśyasyāprameyasya śrūyate vipulo dhvaniḥ
english: Here too the vast resonance of the invisible and immeasurable golden-headed, tawny-haired one who sings is heard.

sanskrit: atra dhvajavatī nāma kumārī harimedhasaḥ ākāśe tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti tasthau sūryasya śāsanāt
english: Here a maiden named Dhvajavatī, daughter of Harimedhas, stood suspended in the sky, halted there by the command of the sun.

sanskrit: atra vāyus tathā vahnir āpaḥ khaṃ caiva gālava āhnikaṃ caiva naiśaṃ ca duḥkhasparśaṃ vimuñcati ataḥ prabhṛti sūryasya tiryag āvartate gatiḥ
english: Here, O Gālava, wind, fire, water, and ether release the touch of pain — both day's and night's; from this point onward the sun's course turns obliquely.

sanskrit: atra jyotīṃṣi sarvāṇi viśanty ādityamaṇḍalam aṣṭāviṃśatirātraṃ ca caṅkramya saha bhānunā niṣpatanti punaḥ sūryāt somasaṃyogayogataḥ
english: Here all the luminaries enter the solar orb, and having wandered together with the sun for twenty-eight nights, they issue forth again from the sun through union with the moon.

sanskrit: atra nityaṃ sravantīnāṃ prabhavaḥ sāgarodayaḥ atra lokatrayasyāpas tiṣṭhanti varuṇāśrayāḥ
english: Here perpetually is the origin of rivers — the rising of the ocean; here the waters of the three worlds rest, sheltered by Varuṇa.

sanskrit: atra pannagarājasyāpy anantasya niveśanam anādinidhanasyātra viṣṇoḥ sthānam anuttamam
english: Here too is the dwelling of Ananta, king of serpents, and here is the unsurpassed abode of Viṣṇu, who has no beginning and no end.

sanskrit: atrānalasakhasyāpi pavanasya niveśanam maharṣeḥ kaśyapasyātra mārīcasya niveśanam
english: Here too is the dwelling of Pavana, friend of fire, and here is the dwelling of the great sage Kaśyapa, son of Marīci.

sanskrit: eṣa te paścimo mārgo digdvāreṇa prakīrtitaḥ brūhi gālava gacchāvo buddhiḥ kā dvijasattama
english: This western path has been described to you through the gateway of the direction; tell me, O Gālava, where shall we go — what is your mind, O foremost of twice-born?

sanskrit: suparṇa uvāca yasmād uttāryate pāpād yasmān niḥśreyaso 'śnute tasmād uttāraṇaphalād uttarety ucyate budhaiḥ
english: Suparṇa said: Because one is lifted from sin here, because one obtains the highest good here, therefore the wise call it uttarā — the north — from the fruit of being uplifted.

sanskrit: uttarasya hiraṇyasya parivāpasya gālava mārgaḥ paścimapūrvābhyāṃ digbhyāṃ vai madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: The path of the northern golden region, O Gālava, is indeed regarded as the middle way between the western and eastern directions.

sanskrit: asyāṃ diśi variṣṭhāyām uttarāyāṃ dvijarṣabha nāsaumyo nāvidheyātmā nādharmyo vasate janaḥ
english: In this most excellent northern direction, O bull among twice-born, no one who is disagreeable, no one of disobedient nature, no unrighteous person dwells.

sanskrit: atra nārāyaṇaḥ kṛṣṇo jiṣṇuś caiva narottamaḥ badaryām āśramapade tathā brahmā ca śāśvataḥ
english: Here dwell Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and the best of men Jiṣṇu at the hermitage of Badarī, and likewise the eternal Brahmā.

sanskrit: atra vai himavatpṛṣṭhe nityam āste maheśvaraḥ atra rājyena viprāṇāṃ candramāś cābhyaṣicyata
english: Here on the slopes of the Himālaya the great lord Maheśvara always abides; here the Moon was anointed with sovereignty over the brahmins.

sanskrit: atra gaṅgāṃ mahādevaḥ patantīṃ gaganāc cyutām pratigṛhya dadau loke mānuṣe brahmavittama
english: Here the great god received the Gaṅgā as she fell, descended from the heavens, and gave her to the human world, O foremost knower of brahman.

sanskrit: atra devyā tapas taptaṃ maheśvaraparīpsayā atra kāmaś ca roṣaś ca śailaś comā ca saṃbabhuḥ
english: Here the goddess performed austerities in her desire to win Maheśvara; here Kāma, Roṣa, the mountain, and Umā all came into being.

sanskrit: atra rākṣasayakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ ca gālava ādhipatyena kailāse dhanado 'py abhiṣecitaḥ
english: Here, O Gālava, Dhanada was anointed with lordship over the rākṣasas, yakṣas, and Gandharvas on Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: atra caitrarathaṃ ramyam atra vaikhānasāśramaḥ atra mandākinī caiva mandaraś ca dvijarṣabha
english: Here is the lovely garden of Caitraratha, here the hermitage of the Vaikhānasas, and here the Mandākinī river and Mount Mandara, O bull among twice-born.

sanskrit: atra saugandhikavanaṃ nairṛtair abhirakṣyate śāḍvalaṃ kadalīskandham atra saṃtānakā nagāḥ
english: Here the Saugandhika forest, lush with grass and stands of plantain, is guarded by the demons of the southwest; here grow the Santānaka trees.

sanskrit: atra saṃyamanityānāṃ siddhānāṃ svairacāriṇām vimānāny anurūpāṇi kāmabhogyāni gālava
english: Here are the celestial chariots suited to the perfected ones who are ever self-restrained and yet wander freely — chariots that fulfil every pleasure, O Gālava.

sanskrit: atra te ṛṣayaḥ sapta devī cārundhatī tathā atra tiṣṭhati vai svātir atrāsyā udayaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Here are those seven sages and the goddess Arundhatī as well; here the star Svāti stands, and here its rising is remembered.

sanskrit: atra yajñaṃ samāruhya dhruvaṃ sthātā pitāmahaḥ jyotīṃṣi candrasūryau ca parivartanti nityaśaḥ
english: Here the grandfather Brahmā, having mounted sacrifice, is established as the fixed Pole Star; the luminaries and the sun and moon revolve around him perpetually.

sanskrit: atra gāyantikādvāraṃ rakṣanti dvijasattamāḥ dhāmā nāma mahātmāno munayaḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: Here the foremost among twice-born guard the gate called Gāyantikā — great-souled sages named Dhāmā, ever truthful in speech.

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ jñāyate sūtir nākṛtir na tapaś citam parivartasahasrāṇi kāmabhogyāni gālava
english: Their birth is not known, nor their form, nor the austerities they have accumulated; thousands of cycles of pleasure await them, O Gālava.

sanskrit: yathā yathā praviśati tasmāt parataraṃ naraḥ tathā tathā dvijaśreṣṭha pravilīyati gālava
english: The further a man ventures beyond that point, O foremost of twice-born, the more he dissolves away, O Gālava.

sanskrit: na tat kena cid anyena gatapūrvaṃ dvijarṣabha ṛte nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ naraṃ vā jiṣṇum avyayam
english: That region has never before been traversed by anyone else, O bull among twice-born, save the divine Nārāyaṇa or Nara, the imperishable Jiṣṇu.

sanskrit: atra kailāsam ity uktaṃ sthānam ailavilasya tat atra vidyutprabhā nāma jajñire 'psaraso daśa
english: Here is that place called Kailāsa, the abode of Ailavila; here ten apsarasas named Vidyutprabhā were born.

sanskrit: atra viṣṇupadaṃ nāma kramatā viṣṇunā kṛtam trilokavikrame brahmann uttarāṃ diśam āśritam
english: Here is what is called Viṣṇupada — the footprint made by Viṣṇu as he strode through the three worlds — situated in the northern direction, O brahmin.

sanskrit: atra rājñā maruttena yajñeneṣṭaṃ dvijottama uśīrabīje viprarṣe yatra jāmbūnadaṃ saraḥ
english: Here King Marutta performed sacrifice, O foremost of twice-born, O seer among sages, at Uśīrabīja, where lies the lake of Jāmbūnada gold.

sanskrit: jīmūtasyātra viprarṣer upatasthe mahātmanaḥ sākṣād dhaimavataḥ puṇyo vimalaḥ kamalākaraḥ
english: Here the sacred, pure, lotus-filled lake of the Himālayas attended in person upon the great-souled seer-sage Jīmūta.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣu ca yat kṛtsnaṃ svantaṃ kṛtvā dhanaṃ mahat vavre vanaṃ maharṣiḥ sa jaimūtaṃ tad vanaṃ tataḥ
english: Having donated all his great wealth to brahmins, that great sage chose the forest; hence that forest became known as Jaimūta — the forest of Jīmūta.

sanskrit: atra nityaṃ diśāpālāḥ sāyaṃ prātar dvijarṣabha kasya kāryaṃ kim iti vai parikrośanti gālava
english: Here the guardians of the directions call out perpetually each morning and evening, O bull among twice-born: "Whose task? What is it?" — O Gālava.

sanskrit: evam eṣā dvijaśreṣṭha guṇair anyair dig uttarā uttareti parikhyātā sarvakarmasu cottarā
english: Thus, O foremost of twice-born, this northern direction is renowned as uttarā — the north — for these and other virtues, and it is uttarā — superior — in all undertakings.

sanskrit: etā vistaraśas tāta tava saṃkīrtitā diśaḥ catasraḥ kramayogena kāmāśāṃ gantum icchasi
english: These four directions have been described to you at length, my friend, in due order; now tell me in which direction you wish to go according to your desire.

sanskrit: udyato 'haṃ dvijaśreṣṭha tava darśayituṃ diśaḥ pṛthivīṃ cākhilāṃ brahmaṃs tasmād āroha māṃ dvija
english: I am ready, O foremost of twice-born, to show you the directions and the entire earth, O brahmin; therefore mount me, O twice-born.

sanskrit: gālava uvāca garutman bhujagendrāre suparṇa vinatātmaja naya māṃ tārkṣya pūrveṇa yatra dharmasya cakṣuṣī
english: Gālava said: O Garuḍa, foe of the serpent lord, O Suparṇa, son of Vinatā, take me eastward, O Tārkṣya, to where the two eyes of dharma are.

sanskrit: pūrvam etāṃ diśaṃ gaccha yā pūrvaṃ parikīrtitā daivatānāṃ hi sāṃnidhyam atra kīrtitavān asi
english: Go first to that eastern direction which was described first; for it is there that you proclaimed the presence of the gods.

sanskrit: atra satyaṃ ca dharmaś ca tvayā samyak prakīrtitaḥ iccheyaṃ tu samāgantuṃ samastair daivatair aham bhūyaś ca tān surān draṣṭum iccheyam aruṇānuja
english: Truth and dharma have been well proclaimed there by you; I desire to come together with all the gods, and to behold those devas once more, O younger brother of Aruṇa.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tam āha vinatāsūnur ārohasveti vai dvijam ārurohātha sa munir garuḍaṃ gālavas tadā
english: Nārada said: The son of Vinatā said to that twice-born: "Mount me"; and then the sage Gālava mounted Garuḍa.

sanskrit: gālava uvāca kramamāṇasya te rūpaṃ dṛśyate pannagāśana bhāskarasyeva pūrvāhṇe sahasrāṃśor vivasvataḥ
english: Gālava said: As you stride forward, O devourer of serpents, your form appears like that of the thousand-rayed Vivasvat in the forenoon.

sanskrit: pakṣavātapraṇunnānāṃ vṛkṣāṇām anugāminām prasthitānām iva samaṃ paśyāmīha gatiṃ khaga
english: I see here the motion of trees driven forward by the wind of your wings, all following together, as if they had set out on a journey, O bird.

sanskrit: sasāgaravanām urvīṃ saśailavanakānanām ākarṣann iva cābhāsi pakṣavātena khecara
english: You seem to be drawing the earth — with its oceans and forests, its mountains, woods, and thickets — toward you with the wind of your wings, O traveller of the sky.

sanskrit: samīnanāganakraṃ ca kham ivāropyate jalam vāyunā caiva mahatā pakṣavātena cāniśam
english: The water with its fish, serpents, and crocodiles seems to be lifted up into the sky by the great wind and by your wing-gust, ceaselessly.

sanskrit: tulyarūpānanān matsyāṃs timimatsyāṃs timiṃgilān nāgāṃś ca naravaktrāṃś ca paśyāmy unmathitān iva
english: I see fish that all look alike, whales that eat fish, creatures that swallow even whales, and serpents with human faces, all churned up as it were.

sanskrit: mahārṇavasya ca ravaiḥ śrotre me badhirīkṛte na śṛṇomi na paśyāmi nātmano vedmi kāraṇam
english: My ears have been deafened by the roar of the great ocean; I neither hear nor see, and I do not know the reason for my own state.

sanskrit: śanaiḥ sādhu bhavān yātu brahmahatyām anusmaran na dṛśyate ravis tāta na diśo na ca khaṃ khaga
english: Please go slowly, keeping in mind the sin of slaying a brahmin; the sun cannot be seen, my friend, nor the directions, nor the sky, O bird.

sanskrit: tama eva tu paśyāmi śarīraṃ te na lakṣaye maṇīva jātyau paśyāmi cakṣuṣī te 'ham aṇḍaja
english: I see only darkness and cannot make out your body; your two eyes I can see, O egg-born, like a pair of precious gems.

sanskrit: śarīre tu na paśyāmi tava caivātmanaś ca ha pade pade tu paśyāmi salilād agnim utthitam
english: I cannot see your body, nor indeed my own; at every step I see fire rising up from the water.

sanskrit: sa me nirvāpya sahasā cakṣuṣī śāmyate punaḥ tan nivarta mahān kālo gacchato vinatātmaja
english: That fire suddenly extinguishes my sight and then it calms; therefore turn back — a great time has passed in our going, O son of Vinatā.

sanskrit: na me prayojanaṃ kiṃ cid gamane pannagāśana saṃnivarta mahāvega na vegaṃ viṣahāmi te
english: I have no purpose left in this journey, O devourer of serpents; turn back, O one of great speed — I cannot bear your velocity.

sanskrit: gurave saṃśrutānīha śatāny aṣṭau hi vājinām ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ śubhrāṇāṃ candravarcasām
english: For I have promised my teacher eight hundred horses here — white horses with one dark ear each, radiant as the moon.
